source.title: Local Linearity of LLMs Enables Activation Steering via Model-Based Linear Optimal Control
source.authors: Julian Skifstad; Xin-Yue-An-Nie Yang; Glen Chou

record.file_problem: The text includes OCR artifacts and flattened tables, but the relevant jailbreaking results and model assignments are readable. The paper text runs through its appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses contrastive mean-difference feature directions and reports how A-LQR steering changes refusal and harmful-request compliance. This is a causal steering test of refusal-related behavior, but it does not perform the original all-layer, all-position projection ablation or test its harmless-request effect.
record.gate_note: The paper reports refusal and attack-success outcomes for its A-LQR and A-LQR+ jailbreaking interventions in Table 3. Other reported outcomes concern toxicity, truthfulness, arbitrary concepts, or local Jacobian linearity and are not rows for these claim versions. The text does not establish that the jailbreaking vector is exactly the original harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction.
record.test_reason: Section 8 steers a per-layer contrastive mean-difference direction, built from AdvBench data, with an LQR feedback controller. It reports refusal score and HarmBench ASR on 104 held-out harmful prompts across five instruct models. This tests V1's claim that suppressing the direction removes refusal, using a different intervention (setpoint steering, not projection ablation). The text does not state the exact contrast set (harmful vs. harmless) used for the refusal direction.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors report that final-token A-LQR matches baselines on refusal score but underperforms on ASR, a pattern they call benign non-refusal. They read this as suggesting that non-refusal and compliance representations are related but not interchangeable in the final-token residual stream. Intervening at all token positions (A-LQR+) matches or beats Adaptive Angular Steering, which they present as state-of-the-art mechanistic jailbreaking.
record.recipe_differences: Uses contrastive mean-difference feature directions, but steers them with an LQR feedback controller and adaptive feature setpoints rather than directly projecting out one refusal direction. A-LQR acts at the final-token position; A-LQR+ acts at all token positions.
record.method_sensitivity: In the jailbreaking evaluation, extending the intervention from the final token to all token positions changes attack success; results also vary across model.
record.problems: The jailbreaking evaluation uses one deterministic evaluation over 104 prompts, with no uncertainty estimates. Refusal is measured by substring matching; the authors note that this can count benign non-refusal as refusal suppression even when the model does not address the harmful request. The study does not establish that its steering vector is the exact single refusal direction in the claim.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported result for the original projection ablation, harmless-request false refusal, or general-capability preservation under the jailbreaking intervention. Other methods in Table 3 are not rows because they do not apply the study's contrastive A-LQR direction.

untested.parts: Projection ablation of the direction at all layers and positions; adding the direction to induce refusal on harmless prompts; capability preservation (no MMLU, perplexity or coherence numbers for the jailbreak runs); whether the steered vector equals the harmful-minus-harmless direction.

record.verdict_notes: Each model has one greedy run over 104 prompts, with no uncertainty reported. Refusal is measured by substring matching, which overstates refusal removal relative to ASR. The AAS and S-PID baselines in Table 3 are correctly excluded as rows. The toxicity, truthfulness and concept experiments do not bear on any version.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test projection of the direction out of every layer and position, inducing refusal on harmless requests, or preservation of general capability under the same refusal intervention.
Does not test whether other attacks suppress the specific refusal direction or whether training against its ablation improves robustness.
Does not test whether refusal is represented by an affine set, cone, or multiple directions.
Does not separately measure harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
No transfer test of the refusal direction across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct stages.
Does not compare refusal-training procedures or training stages for whether a removable direction exists.

relationships.condition: A-LQR+ (all token positions) on Gemma-2-9B, Llama-3.2-3B, Qwen2.5-14B and Llama-3.1-8B Instruct; substring refusal for both variants on all five models
relationships.reason: Steering the contrastive direction drives refusal to 0 in every model (r2, r4, r6, r8, r10, r12, r14, r16, r18, r20). With all-token steering, ASR is 0.91–0.97 (r3, r7, r11, r15).
relationships.display_finding: Steering reduced substring-detected refusal to 0 in every model, with all-token steering achieving attack success of 0.91–0.97.

relationships.condition: Final-token-only steering (A-LQR) on all models, and A-LQR+ on Qwen2.5-3B Instruct
relationships.reason: Refusal phrases vanish but ASR stays at 0.14–0.86, which the authors call benign non-refusal (r1, r5, r9, r13, r17). Qwen2.5-3B reaches only 0.77 even with all-token steering (r19).
relationships.display_finding: ASR remained 0.14–0.86 despite disappearing refusal phrases, and Qwen2.5-3B reached only 0.77 even with steering across all tokens.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: A-LQR and A-LQR+ on the five tested instruct models, harmful AdvBench prompts
reader_labels.reason: The substring refusal score falls to 0 for both interventions in every tested model (r2, r4, r6, r8, r10, r12, r14, r16, r18, r20). This supports steering-related reduction in measured refusal, not the original projection-ablation claim.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Harmful-request compliance under A-LQR, especially Qwen2.5-3B Instruct
reader_labels.reason: Refusal-score reduction does not always yield harmful compliance: ASR is 0.1442 for Qwen2.5-3B and is incomplete for several other A-LQR settings; the authors describe benign non-refusal (r1, r5, r9, r13, r17). The all-token variant raises ASR, but remains incomplete for Qwen2.5-3B (r19).
